A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CONCEPTVECTORS research. All 23 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark validation, unlearning evaluations, jailbreak experiments and Needle ablations on LLaMA and OLMo.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds RMU comparisons and automated-jailbreak activation measurements.

M1.justification: v3 introduces RMU (enhanced), adapting layer selection to the concept-vector layer and its two predecessors. Benchmark construction remains stable. Needle's description omits its former localized gradient-ascent step, but Appendix E still says that step was used, so an actual Needle procedure change remains unresolved.

E1.justification: v3 adds model-optimized adversarial inputs through GCG and AutoDAN to the existing jailbreak scenarios. The 285 concept vectors, model coverage and QA/completion tasks remain unchanged. Appendix A.8 discusses finer-grained unlearning without evaluating that new task.

E2.justification: RMU and RMU (enhanced) join the evaluated comparators in v3 Table 1 and Figures 3, 5 and 6. The previous gradient, preference-optimization and MEMIT comparators are retained, making this a limited expansion of the comparison set.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 introduces automated prompt optimization against unlearned models, targeting the vanilla models' original answers. RMU comparisons add fixed versus concept-relative editing-layer settings. Existing data splits, evaluation metrics and the ten-concept jailbreak design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 extends the concept-reactivation analysis to GCG and AutoDAN and compares fixed versus concept-localized RMU interventions. The original causal validation, QA-quality review, Needle component/loss ablations and Jaccard-versus-jailbreak analysis remain, including material moved into appendices.

E5.justification: The activation-distribution boxplots and Figure 9 error bars, including discussion of standard deviation, are retained. Neither version provides additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Needle's target/unrelated QA BLEU changes from 0.462/0.534 to 0.532/0.947 for LLaMA and from 0.313/0.447 to 0.331/0.786 for OLMo, materially changing its reported specificity. Other existing main-table rows are unchanged; RMU results and automated-attack activations are added. Figure 5 also changes, apparently reusing existing methods' BLEU curves under a ROUGE-L caption. Needle's revisions are not established same-setting gains: its procedure is unclear and Figure 6 retains the earlier points.

T1.justification: The MLP decomposition, vocabulary projections and concept-vector definitions are retained. New discussion of a necessary condition and lower bound is conceptual; no new formal assumptions, theorem, derivation or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central claims about residual knowledge, intrinsic evaluation and jailbreak robustness remain. The introduction qualifies vectors' effects on unrelated concepts from no influence to minimal influence and specifies the novelty claim as parameter-based internal evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 removes the characterization of Needle performance as an upper bound, expands discussion of partial and mixed concept representations, and adds finer-grained and rare-knowledge applicability qualifications. Its results discussion newly emphasizes Needle's specificity and explains RMU through activation disruption.

D1.justification: v3 adds screening agreement requirements, RMU layer-selection details and automated-attack optimization targets, while referring remaining new hyperparameters to the cited methods. The repository link, hardware and existing tuning information persist. Omitting Needle's gradient-ascent step from Appendix B reduces clarity despite its retention in Appendix E.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning and citations around representation engineering, refusal directions, representation noising, circuit breakers and AutoDAN. Existing research positioning largely remains; publication updates and the duplicated GCG reference do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial passages are rewritten. Related work moves near the beginning, detailed unlearning methods and QA-quality analysis move to appendices, and the standalone reproducibility section disappears. The title, affiliations, conclusion and ethics presentation are also revised.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 becomes vertical, dataset tables move to the appendix, comparison tables gain rows or columns, and Figures 3, 5 and 6 are redrawn with expanded legends and markers. These are extensive visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: RMU comparisons, automated-attack activation tests and clearer scope qualifications strengthen v3. However, its revised Needle table conflicts with Figure 6, its method description leaves gradient ascent unresolved, and Figure 5 appears to reuse BLEU curves under a ROUGE-L caption. These new inconsistencies affect central results and reproducibility, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
